plan.summary: This 1-4 block is an off-camp boxing build with two full-body sessions each week. Week 1 establishes training baselines using bodyweight strength tests that fit your equipment, then Weeks 2-4 build lower-body strength, upper-body pushing and pulling strength, trunk stiffness, and repeatable power with simple jumps, explosive push-up work, and short conditioning. The bigger 12-week cycle starts with this building block, then intensifies in Weeks 5-8, then shifts toward sharper speed and power expression in Weeks 9-12. Review progress and recovery at the end of Week 4 before the next block is set.

phaseOverview.label: Building
phaseOverview.focus: Build general strength, trunk stiffness, simple explosive ability, and repeatable conditioning with bodyweight-only work.

phaseOverview.label: Intensifying
phaseOverview.focus: Progress unilateral strength, harder bodyweight loading, and sharper power output while keeping recovery manageable around boxing practice.

phaseOverview.label: Expressing
phaseOverview.focus: Keep strength with lower volume and express it through faster, cleaner jumps, push-up power, and boxing-relevant speed endurance.

exercises.name: 1a. Countermovement Jump
exercises.notes: Reset between reps and jump as high as you can. Land softly and stop if height drops off.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you have limited ceiling control or want a simpler jump.

substitutionOptions.name: Box Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a low safe box and step down each rep.

exercises.name: 2. Rear-Foot-Elevated Split Squat
exercises.notes: Warm up with easier split squats, then build to one hard clean set per side. This establishes your baseline for future progression. Use full control, stay tall, and stop one rep before form breaks.

strengthAssessment.prompt: Warm up progressively, then work up to one hard set of 6-10 reps per side using a version that lets you keep balance and depth. Log reps completed and the exact variation used so the app can track your baseline.

performanceTarget.prompt: Beat the quality of this best test set in a later block by using a harder variation, cleaner depth, or more reps with the same variation.

substitutionOptions.name: Split Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if rear-foot-elevated setup is awkward.

substitutionOptions.name: Shrimp Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you are very comfortable with unilateral bodyweight strength and want a harder option.

exercises.name: 3a. Push-Up
exercises.notes: Leave 2 reps in reserve on each set. Keep ribs down and move as one piece.

substitutionOptions.name: Feet-Elevated Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if standard push-ups are too easy.

substitutionOptions.name: Incline Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if standard push-ups are too hard to keep clean.

exercises.name: 3b. Doorframe Row
exercises.notes: Use a very secure setup. Pull elbows back and pause briefly at the top.

substitutionOptions.name: Towel Row Around Pole
substitutionOptions.notes: Use only if the anchor is solid and safe.

substitutionOptions.name: Table Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you have a sturdy heavy table.

exercises.name: 4. Side Plank
exercises.notes: Make a straight line from head to heel. Do not let the top hip roll back.

substitutionOptions.name: Long-Lever Side Plank
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this for a harder trunk challenge.

substitutionOptions.name: Copenhagen Side Plank Short Lever
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you tolerate adductor work well.

exercises.name: 5. Tempo Running Intervals
exercises.notes: Run 8 rounds of 45 seconds at a steady hard pace with 45 seconds easy walk. Stay smooth and nasal-breathing if possible early, then finish the last 2 rounds strong.

exercises.name: 1a. Snap Down to Vertical Jump
exercises.notes: Stick the snap down, then jump fast. Keep contacts crisp and land under control.

substitutionOptions.name: Countermovement Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the snap down rhythm feels awkward.

exercises.name: 1b. Plyometric Push-Up
exercises.notes: Explode off the floor with full intent. Stop before height or speed drops.

substitutionOptions.name: Hands-Release Fast Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if leaving the floor is too aggressive.

substitutionOptions.name: Incline Plyometric Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you need a lower-impact version.

exercises.name: 2. Push-Up
exercises.notes: Warm up with easy sets, then perform one all-out clean set. This establishes your baseline for future progression. Stop when posture or range breaks.

strengthAssessment.prompt: Warm up progressively, then perform one top set for as many clean reps as possible. Log the rep total and the exact variation used so the app can track your baseline.

performanceTarget.prompt: Try to improve this best test set later with more clean reps or a harder variation.

substitutionOptions.name: Feet-Elevated Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if standard push-ups are too easy to test meaningfully.

substitutionOptions.name: Incline Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you cannot keep clean full-range standard reps.

exercises.name: 3a. Single-Leg Hip Bridge
exercises.notes: Drive through the heel and pause for one second at the top. Keep the pelvis level.

substitutionOptions.name: Hip Bridge
substitutionOptions.notes: Use bilateral reps if single-leg control is poor.

substitutionOptions.name: Hamstring Walkout
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you want a stronger hamstring emphasis.

exercises.name: 3b. Doorframe Row
exercises.notes: Stay rigid through the trunk and pull shoulder blades back without shrugging.

substitutionOptions.name: Table Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you have a secure setup.

substitutionOptions.name: Towel Row Around Pole
substitutionOptions.notes: Use only with a safe fixed anchor.

exercises.name: 4. Hollow Body Hold
exercises.notes: Flatten the low back to the floor and breathe shallow behind the brace.

substitutionOptions.name: Dead Bug
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the hollow hold makes you lose lumbar position.

substitutionOptions.name: V-Sit Hold
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you need a harder trunk option.

exercises.name: 5. Shuttle Runs
exercises.notes: Run 10 rounds of 15 seconds hard and 45 seconds walk-back recovery. Keep the first 6 rounds controlled and the last 4 sharp.
